LandGuard Open control center

Safer Lands. Stronger Tomorrows.

One risk picture for authorities and residents.

LandGuard watches the slopes of Northeast India from recorded landslides, live rainfall, terrain and satellite observations. Authorities see it in this control center; residents see the same data and receive the same alerts in the LandGuard Android app.

Where we monitor

Monitored areas are not hand-picked. They are clusters of landslides recorded in the NASA Global Landslide Catalog across all eight Northeast states — Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura. Any other location can be analysed on demand.

What the risk index reads

Every input carries its source and the time it was observed. If an input is unavailable it is left out and the page says so — nothing is estimated or simulated in its place.

  • Landslide recordNASA Global Landslide Catalog (historical)
  • Rainfall & soil moistureOpen-Meteo weather models, hourly
  • Slope & elevationCopernicus GLO-90 DEM
  • Vegetation changeESA Sentinel-2 L2A (NDVI)
  • Ground surface changeESA Sentinel-1 RTC (C-band SAR)
  • ALOS-4 PALSAR-3Not publicly available — shown as unavailable

Risk levels

The same four levels and thresholds are used by the backend, this control center and the Android app.

Critical75–100 · act now
High50–74 · prepare to act
Moderate25–49 · watch closely
Low0–24 · routine monitoring

How an alert reaches people

1 · Authority issues the alert in the control center (critical and high alerts need an incident commander).
2 · Backend stores it with one alert ID and an expiry time.
3 · Firebase Cloud Messaging delivers it to every registered LandGuard phone.
4 · Nearby Connections lets phones pass it on to nearby LandGuard users who have no internet.
5 · Phones confirm receipt back to the control center when they are online.
LandGuard — landslide intelligence for Northeast India.
